card.name: Buyn Bi
card.era: Traditional roots in Bakhsy/shamanic culture; staged version created in the Soviet era
card.tagline: Kazakh 'dance of the joints' rooted in shamanic movement
card.profile: Buyn Bi (Kazakh 'buwin biyi', 'dance of joints') is a Kazakh dance based on rhythmic movements of the shoulder and hand joints, convulsive stretching of the limbs and deep bends of the body (ResearchGate; Wikipedia). Scholars including dance researcher Rosa Vercoe argue it shares deep origins with the dance now widely known as Kara Jorga, tracing it to Bakhsy (shaman) culture (Central Asia Program). A staged Buyn Bi was created by choreographer Olga Vsevolodskaya-Golushkevich for the Altynai folk dance ensemble, working under ethnographer Uzbekali Dzhanibekov, and was performed by dancer Talant Kylyshbaev (ResearchGate). Its elements survive in the Kazakh male dance curriculum as the section 'Buyn oinatu' ('the game of joints') (Central Asia Program).
card.insight: Some Kazakh scholars contend the name 'Kara Zhorga' was effectively borrowed for a dance their ancestors actually called 'Buyn bi', making the two closely intertwined rather than wholly separate traditions (Central Asia Program).
card.image_significance: The steppe 'dance of joints'. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Kazakhstan.
